title: Concord, Massachusetts
seoTitle: Charter Bus to Concord, Massachusetts: Group Guide
excerpt: A charter bus to Concord, Massachusetts covers the Revolution and the writers in one day. The sites, the walking, and how to pair it with Lexington.

heroImage.alt: The wooden Old North Bridge over the Concord River with the Minute Man statue beyond

extraImage.alt: Walden Pond ringed by autumn woodland under a clear sky

body.text: Two things happened in Concord. In April 1775 colonial militia turned back British regulars at the North Bridge, and the first shots of a revolution were fired. Sixty years later a group of writers — Emerson, Thoreau, Hawthorne, the Alcotts — settled within a mile of each other and reshaped American literature. A charter bus to Concord gets a group to both, which is a rare amount of significance for one small town.
The Revolutionary sites

Minute Man National Historical Park runs along the road the British retreated down, from Concord back toward Lexington. The Old North Bridge is the centrepiece — a wooden span over the Concord River with Daniel Chester French's Minute Man statue on the far bank and Emerson's 'shot heard round the world' inscribed at its base.

The park's visitor centres are free and the Battle Road Trail follows five miles of the retreat route. A group does not need to walk all of it; the bridge and the North Bridge Visitor Center make a solid ninety minutes, and rangers run programmes that are considerably better than reading the plaques.
The literary sites

items: Orchard House: where Louisa May Alcott wrote and set Little Women, with much of the family's furniture still in place. Timed tours, small rooms, and group slots that must be booked ahead.
The Wayside: home to the Alcotts, then Hawthorne. Next door to Orchard House and part of the national park.
The Ralph Waldo Emerson House: the centre of the Transcendentalist circle, open seasonally.
Sleepy Hollow Cemetery: Emerson, Thoreau, Hawthorne and the Alcotts are all buried within a few steps of each other on Authors Ridge. A short uphill walk and a genuinely striking place.
Walden Pond: a mile and a half south, with a replica of Thoreau's cabin and a path around the water. The pond is a state reservation with a strict visitor cap in summer.

body.text: Book the house museums before the vehicle

Orchard House in particular runs on timed tours through small rooms, and a group of forty will be split across several slots. Walden Pond limits how many people are admitted at once and closes the gate when it fills, which catches out groups arriving on a hot July afternoon without a reservation.
Fix those times first and build the coach schedule around them. It is the difference between a smooth day and a group standing outside a full car park.
Which charter bus suits a Concord day

items: Forty to fifty-six: a full-size [charter bus](/fleet/charter-buses) is the standard school-group vehicle, and the national park sites have coach parking.
Twenty to thirty-two: a [mini bus](/fleet/mini-buses) is easier at the smaller house museums and around the town centre, where streets are narrow and colonial.
Twenty-eight to sixty: a [school bus](/fleet/school-buses) is the economical choice for districts within about ninety minutes.
Ten to fourteen: a [sprinter van](/fleet/sprinter-vans) suits a literary society or a small tour.

body.text: Concord is one of the most-visited school destinations in New England, and our [school trip transportation](/services/school-trips) quotes include the insurance certificates and driver documentation districts require.
Pairing Concord with Lexington

The two towns share one story and are fifteen minutes apart, so most history itineraries do both. Lexington Green, where the first shots were exchanged at dawn, comes first chronologically, and running the day in that order — Lexington, the Battle Road, then the North Bridge — makes the narrative land properly for a school group.
That full sequence is a comfortable day. Adding Walden Pond and Orchard House on top makes it a long one, and something will get rushed.
Getting there

[Concord](/locations/massachusetts/concord) is about twenty-five miles north-west of [Boston](/locations/massachusetts/boston), typically forty minutes outside rush hour and rather longer inside it. [Lexington](/locations/massachusetts/lexington) is fifteen minutes away, [Cambridge](/locations/massachusetts/cambridge) around half an hour, and [Lowell](/locations/massachusetts/lowell) twenty-five minutes north for groups adding the industrial history site.

Groups searching for charter bus rental near me for a Patriots' Day trip should book very early. The April anniversary weekend brings reenactments, road closures and the heaviest demand of the year in both towns.

A note on Walden Pond that catches groups out: it is a working swimming beach in summer as well as a literary site, and the parking reservation system exists because the reservation fills. If Thoreau's cabin is on your itinerary, book the slot when you book the coach, and be aware that a group arriving without one in July will be turned away at the gate regardless of how far they have travelled.
When to go

April through June and September through October are ideal, with October adding autumn colour along the Battle Road and around Walden. The house museums are seasonal — several close or reduce hours from November to March — so a winter visit is limited to the outdoor sites, which are free, open and quiet.
Booking the trip
